name: Processed aconite root (Radix Aconiti Lateralis Preparata)
short: Aconite alkaloids are cardiotoxins and neurotoxins: poisoning reviews report deaths from ventricular arrhythmias and asystole, linked to overdose and poor processing or boiling of the root.
text: Aconite roots contain aconitine and related alkaloids, which a toxicology review describes as highly toxic cardiotoxins and neurotoxins; in traditional Chinese medicine the roots are processed to reduce the toxic alkaloid content, but the review states that a larger than recommended dose and inadequate processing increase the risk of poisoning. The review describes poisoning with numbness and tingling, muscle weakness, low blood pressure, chest pain, palpitations, slow or fast heart rhythms including ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation, and nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and diarrhoea; it gives the main causes of death as refractory ventricular arrhythmias and asystole, with an overall in-hospital mortality of 5.5%. A review of 12 fatal cases published between 1992 and 2011 identified poor post-harvest processing, greater than recommended doses and inadequate boiling of processed roots during decoction as important contributory factors, and a review of reports from Hong Kong, Taiwan, China and Korea also named tinctures (herbal medicinal wine), crude roots, unsupervised use, and contamination or mix-up with aconite roots. A case report states that aconite root is the herb that most commonly induces severe adverse effects in Hong Kong and China, and describes a 92-year-old woman with life-threatening bradycardia and hypotension starting 1 hour after she drank a herbal decoction containing Fuzi, an aconite root; she recovered after 25 hours of treatment. This evidence comes from reviews of poisoning cases and case reports, not from trials. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
